# C1 coverage ledger

Snapshot: 2026-11-03. C1b release reconciliation and existing-page review completed. Counts describe this writing ledger, not release acceptance or proof that the product has no other behavior.

Each row is a writing obligation, ordered by section. Sources retain the original record identities; merged IDs are recorded in the surviving Source cell and `_coverage/notes/C1b-RELEASES/semantic-merges.json`. A journey appears once under `journeys`; its variants remain capability/rule obligations. Several readers may share an item. Counts use the least complete reader judgment: uncovered before partly before covered. `not for readers` preserves excluded or superseded evidence without making it a writing task.

Covered judgments cite current page text. Partly judgments identify a specific missing clause, task or screen wording; they no longer mean merely that a page was not read. Existing non-AI pages referenced by those judgments were read in full. Coverage is a documentation judgment, not runtime verification. The `after 0.16` AI/agent inventory is retained unchanged; digests and following are current work. A few older AI rows retain their original generic judgment under that explicit deferral.

Inputs: PROMISES.md, BEHAVIOUR-RULES.md, OUTLINE.md, NOT-YET-COVERED.md, MODEL-EDITOR-INVENTORY.md, UI-INVENTORY-SETTINGS.md, UI-INVENTORY-DATA.md, ../_coverage/restored/INVENTORY.md and docs/product-functionality/USER_JOURNEYS.md. Old page-existence audits were reconciled against current pages, not repeated as product facts. Planned homes follow OUTLINE.md. Detailed release resolutions and page judgments are saved under `_coverage/notes/C1b-RELEASES/`.

Counts (covered / partly / uncovered / after 0.16; not for readers separately):

- about: 0 / 0 / 43 / 1; not for readers: 1.
- use: 304 / 104 / 298 / 139; not for readers: 72.
- model: 174 / 119 / 481 / 27; not for readers: 18.
- administer: 123 / 65 / 61 / 31; not for readers: 9.
- run: 125 / 23 / 13 / 58; not for readers: 35.
- integrate: 0 / 1 / 645 / 43; not for readers: 30.
- examples: 4 / 1 / 1 / 0; not for readers: 0.
- journeys: 18 / 0 / 29 / 9; not for readers: 1.

Total: 3106 rows; 183 deferred AI/agent release-evidence leads retained. Stable IDs are not renumbered after merging.

| C0390 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: A record named in words is found by the engine, in the database, in the context asked about. The model gives a name; the engine looks among the proper types (those the relationship reaches for "is any of", those its records can stand under for under and notUnder): the exact name, ignoring case, first; otherwise the one record whose name contains it. None, or several, is a part in notExpressed with the reason (up to five names), never a guess. A record created in a change set is found there and not live.. The model sees no record, so it cannot choose one. A wrong guess would change a list silently. /. | rule | steward | use | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-AG-D36; PL §0.16 plan AG-D36 | uncovered → use/change-sets — reconcile the cited release evidence before writing |
| C0391 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: An assistant reads and writes only change sets its own principal created; any other answers CHANGE_SET_NOT_FOUND. A person's own change set counts, so "add these to my change set" works. Narrower than the API, where anyone holding the group may write to any open change set.. AG-D8: text in a record could otherwise steer an assistant into a colleague's change set, under review by someone who did not ask for it. Cost: an assistant cannot help on a colleague's change set. Opening this later is additive. | rule | steward | use | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-AG-D27; PL §0.16 plan AG-D27 | after 0.16 |

| C0393 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: Eleven tools, all needing Work in change sets in the workspace. Reading: my_change_sets (open ones, with state and version), read_change_set (version, release, submission state, the last decision's comment), change_set_changes (rows, kind records or relationships, paged), validate_change_set. Writing: create_change_set, add_record, change_record, set_field, add_relation, change_relation, submit_change_set. Every write names changeSetId and expectedChangeSetVersion, and a change to a row its version too. changeSetId joins find_records, read_record and describe_type (AG-D22), which then read that change set and its pinned release. A write answers with IDs and the new versions.. The scope, with what an assistant needs to know that a person sent it back and why. describe_type must read the pinned release, or a change set on another release would be filled from the wrong model. Choosing a release needs mode. | rule | steward | use | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-AG-D26; PL §0.16 plan AG-D26 | after 0.16 |

| C1234 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: (Revised 2026-11-01: the fields are also every relationship of the type.) A field or condition the list does not offer, or a value its validation refuses, makes the whole answer a failed call. The fields are the view's filterFields and, live, the two stamps. Each filter then goes through the list's own validation by building the list's statement with it; a refusal marks the call recorded as answered as failed (kind malformed), and the route answers 502 QUERY_TRANSLATION_FAILED with details.callId, as it does for a provider that fails. Nothing comes back to apply, and the box keeps its words.. The model's answer is data to check, never a guess to repair (AP1). | C1281 | Release evidence awaiting reconciliation: Rule: Named by the definition, not by the workspace. lookup_<key>, with a required workspace argument listing the workspaces the caller may read it in. Workspaces whose definitions are equal share one tool. Where a key differs between them, or the name would pass 48 characters, the name ends in a short hash of the definition. Hyphens stay; the characters allowed in a key are all legal in a name.. One tool per workspace would multiply the list for no gain when many workspaces run one model. 48 leaves room for Claude Code's prefix under Claude's 64. The list is read per caller, which _run already allows for. /. | rule | steward | use | PROMISES.md unreconciled PL-AG-D20; PL §0.16 plan AG-D20 | uncovered → use/workspaces — reconcile the cited release evidence before writing |
